the two STIM1 and Orai1 proteins are required for the generation of the Ca2+-signal that regulates a number of physiological processes in the cell.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms that regulate the activity of Ca2+ channels in the plasma membrane of cells.
the regulation and modulation of SOCE.
the regulation of intracellular Ca(2+) signaling processes in various cell types and tissues.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SOCE is an important Ca2+ signaling mechanism in cells and that the STIM proteins and Orai1 channels are critical for its generation.
SOCE is a very complex process and that it is regulated in a highly tissue-specific manner.
the STIM1/Orai1 complex is the major SOCE pathway and that the STIM2/Orai1 complex may have an important role under certain conditions.
